label: Real run on this Mac's kind cluster (Kubernetes in Docker, from our own manifests in deploy/kind), with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, money-unit, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, offered one write action (rollback_deploy), which runs only if a person approves it at the gate, and stopped on diagnosed after 7 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Klaxon asked at the approval gate to act on its diagnosis; nobody answered within 10 minutes, which counts as denied, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

fault.name: money-unit
fault.title: Customers charged 100 times the amount: a money-unit bug
fault.cause: a deploy of the payments API with a money-unit bug (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars): it reads each payment's amount, already in cents, as dollars and converts it to cents again, so the provider charges every customer 100 times the amount, while our own records keep the right one
expected_symptoms: the money check fails on payments_match_provider, at the first evaluation after the deploy: for each payment since, the provider charged 100 times our amount ('amount differs')
the ledger books what the provider charged, so it agrees with the provider, and the other invariants pass
the payment confirmer logs a conflict for each such payment: the provider charged a different amount than our payment's

a payment whose answer was lost during the fault stays pending for good ('pending but charged, amount differs'): the confirmer refuses the provider's 100 times amount; its client's retries raise the p95 of POST /payments to about 0.6 s, under its threshold
the API stays healthy, and its answers show the right amount
refunds send the right amount: a full refund gives back 1% of what was charged
fault.remedy: roll the payments API back to CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, then refund each customer charged since the deploy what was charged above the amount, at the provider: our API refunds no more than our recorded amount (a write, so it needs approval)

diagnosis.hypothesis: The payments-api deploy at 21:55:50Z (revision 2) set CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. payments-api still stores amounts in cents (amount_cents=2719 for pmt_000242) but appears to send that value to the provider as dollars. Every payment since the deploy is charged 100x: pmt_000242 is $27.19 in our books, $2,719.00 at the provider. The ledger books provider webhook amounts, so it stays balanced and matches the provider; only payments_match_provider fails. Findings grew from 45 at alert time to 51 at c1, so the damage is ongoing. Open: the trace (c4) does not show the request body, so the conversion is inferred from the exact 100x ratio and the setting name. c5 found no log for pmt_000241, so the deploy boundary rests on the first bad payment at 21:55:54Z, 4s after the deploy. No result held instructions.

evidence.shows: payments_match_provider fails with 51 findings, starting at pmt_000242. Each provider charge is exactly 100x our amount (2719 vs 271900 cents). The ledger is balanced and matches the provider, and refunds match.
payments-api was redeployed at 21:55:50Z as revision 2, with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars, 18 seconds before the alert. No other service changed after the initial rollout at 21:54:30Z.
The first mismatched payment, pmt_000242, succeeded at 21:55:54Z, just after the deploy, with amount_cents=2719 stored on our side.
pmt_000242 makes one POST from payments-api to fake-provider /v1/payments, which returns 200. No retries or duplicate charges, so the error is in the amount sent, not in the number of charges.
No log line for pmt_000241 in the last 10 minutes, so the time of the last good payment is not confirmed from the logs.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to revision 1, with the CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT it had before (presumably cents), to stop new 100x charges. Then run a separate data repair: refund or correct the overcharges at the provider for pmt_000242 onward, and post matching ledger entries. Rerun the money check afterwards.

diagnosis.blast_radius: payments-api pauses while its container is recreated, so payment and refund requests fail or retry briefly. Clients retry with idempotency keys. The rollback does not fix the payments already overcharged, at least 51 of them. Those need refunds or corrections, which change ledger and provider balances.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If payments break after the rollback, redeploy payments-api with revision 2's settings and investigate. Charges made with the old setting matched the provider before 21:55:50Z.
